subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Floating Bridges: Roads on Water
description: A micro-lesson that makes Floating Bridges: Roads on Water usable.

hook.text: Seattle's SR 520 bridge floats on Lake Washington. It doesn't touch the lakebed at all.

buildup.text: Pontoon bridges use hollow concrete boxes that displace water. Buoyancy supports the roadway above.

discovery.text: Norway plans a floating tunnel under the Sognefjord. It would hang suspended in water 1,200 meters deep.

twist.text: Waves, currents, and storms all try to move floating bridges. Anchors and mooring cables hold them steady.

climax.text: Floating bridges cost less than deep-water foundations. Where bedrock is too far down, floating wins.

punchline.text: When the bottom is too deep, the answer is to stay on top.

quiz.question: Why are floating bridges used instead of conventional ones in some locations?
options: They are always cheaper regardless of water depth
They avoid the need for foundations in very deep water
They are temporary and can be removed after a few years
